english.title: Breach safeguards relating to examination of material - bulk personal dataset - Part 7 Investigatory Powers Act 2016
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) deliberately selected for examination data, namely **(..SPECIFY DATA..), contained in a bulk personal dataset retained in reliance on a

(A)_[class]_
(B)_[specific]_

BPD warrant, in breach of a requirement specified in section 224(2) of the Investigatory Powers Act, namely **(..SPECIFY REQUIREMENT..), knowing or believing that the selection of that data was in breach of that requirement
english.legislation: Contrary to section 224(1) and (4) of the Investigatory Powers Act 2016.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
selects for examination data contained in a bulk personal dataset retained in reliance on a class BPD warrant/specific BPD warrant
knowing or believing that the selection of that data was in breach of a requirement specified in section 224(2)
deliberately selected that data in breach of that requirement

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
INDICTMENT: 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Note:
In relation to an offence committed before paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020 comes into force (01/12/20), the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.
Time limit for prosecutions:
None
